For fleets

The office, in the same app as the cab

STONEMILES's company layer gives owners and dispatch a live view of the fleet — and runs the load itself: the broker sends, the desk accepts and assigns a driver, the driver runs it, the receiver confirms, and the delivery seals itself into the Library. All without ever reaching into a driver's private messages or off-duty life.

Owner portal

Every truck, trip, and sealed record across the fleet in one place — IFTA totals, settlements, and exports for the whole company, not one phone at a time.

Driver profiles

Each driver carries a profile built from sealed records — trips, on-time seals, safety scores, and academy completions that follow the driver, not the truck. With “Show my truck & trailer on my profile” on, the profile also shows a truck row — year, make and model with up to 5 truck photos — and a trailer row — year, make and model with up to 5 trailer photos. VIN, plate and unit number never show.

STONEMILES Board

The fleet's shared board: sealed deliveries, clean-week streaks, and season standings posted where the whole company can see them.

Company chats

A company-wide chat and an Owner & All Drivers chat, plus driver groups and direct messages. DMs stay private — company members can never read a driver's private messages.

Fleet dispatch · Live

The dispatch desk

The newest build puts the whole load on the desk: broker sends → desk accepts → driver assigned → driver runs it → receiver confirms on the link → the delivery seals itself → everything lands in the Library, printable, emailable, downloadable.

The fleet inbox

Loads sent through the broker send door — no account, just your fleet’s code or link — land in your desk inbox as offered loads, addressed to your fleet only. Loads your brokers post to the loadboard stay on the board for owner-operators to grab.

Accept & assign to driver

Review an offered load, accept it, and assign it to a driver from the fleet desk. Trucks are ranked by the real empty miles they’d drive to the pickup — a truck already under load is measured from where its current route ends. The driver gets the full load on their phone and runs it with the sealed trip underneath — the desk follows it live the whole way.

Suggested next load

Inside the fleet board, each driver gets ranked next-load suggestions with the reasons printed across four legs — deadhead, calendar availability, home-time, and sealed hours. A leg whose facts are missing reads “not checked” — never assumed. One tap routes into the normal offer / assign flow and every gate still runs — qualification file, home-time and dispatch mode — so a suggestion never puts an unqualified driver on a load: they can be suggested and still be refused at assignment, with the plain reason.

Fleet live board

The fleet’s owner and dispatch seats get a live board of their own drivers: status cards with driver, truck, current lane and plain status, stops, route end + ETA, and last location with its freshness printed. Only your own fleet sees it — never another fleet, never public — and off-duty locations stay private.

Tracking links for brokers & shippers

A driver or the fleet desk can create a per-load tracking link to send a broker or shipper: lane, stops, ETA, status, and the truck’s location with freshness. It ends at delivery, can be revoked anytime, and never shows the rate or any money. Check calls post themselves: load status updates are posted automatically from the load’s sealed records to its tracking page — no driver taps, every update backed by the sealed record it came from. Anything the system isn’t sure about goes to a human exception queue with the evidence attached — never guessed, never posted on a guess. The rate is never part of what goes out. The tracking page shows the paperwork stage too — received → confirmed → sent → invoiced → paid — so the broker can see the POD is in and the invoice is cut, never the rate.

The recruiting door — your own application link

Every fleet gets its own application link. A driver applies with no account — name, contact, CDL class, experience and a short note — and hears back the moment the application lands: an honest acknowledgement in the fleet’s own words that promises a review, nothing more. On the desk, applications move through a simple pipeline — new → contacted → interview → road test → hired or declined — and desk notes stay internal. Mark one hired and the driver gets a pending invite through the same invite system as everyone else — no new account path. Applicant details never land on the sealed chain; only stage moves do.

Delivered, with the proof attached

When the receiver confirms — on the receive link, on the driver’s phone, or on a paper BOL the driver uploads — the load flips to delivered at the desk with the signed proof attached, an exception flag showing if damage or shortage was noted. On the link, the receiver signs by typing their name or drawing their signature — a drawn signature prints on the signed POD, and the sealed record notes how they signed. The sealed delivery files itself into the fleet’s Library.

Two broker doors, one desk. The send door is for directed work — a broker aims a load at your fleet and nobody else sees it. Broker accounts are for the open board — posted loads any owner-operator can claim. Both doors feed the same chain: accept, assign, run, confirm, seal, Library.
Broker identity, checked every tender. Every broker carries an identity record — legal business name, MC number, BMC-84 bond and authority status — and every tender is re-screened against it: an expired bond, a bond under the federal minimum, or revoked or inactive authority blocks the load with a plain reason. Carriers see the broker’s legal name, MC, bond status and verification status on the load before they take it, a carrier who accepts a load can’t re-post it, and each broker keeps their own private 371.3 record file. The status is labelled honestly — identity on file vs checked by a verification source — and nothing is called verified that wasn’t checked.

Qualification files — the Desk checks before it assigns

Every driver carries a 49 CFR 391 qualification file on the Desk — application, CDL, medical certificate, road test, employment history, annual MVR review, the annual violation record, Clearinghouse query log and training, with documents in the vault. Employment history and the annual violation record are required parts of the file — a file missing either one is incomplete, and dispatch stays blocked until it isn’t.

Status from what’s on file

Qualification is computed from what is actually on file and in date — not from a checkbox. The file keeps itself: fleets see CDL, medical and MVR review expiries ahead of time, with warnings at 60, 30 and 7 days. The annual Clearinghouse query goes overdue after 12 months — and an overdue query leaves the file incomplete.

No load for an unqualified driver

Dispatch will not assign or release a claim to a driver with an expired CDL or medical, an MVR review over 12 months old, a Clearinghouse query over 12 months old, a prohibited Clearinghouse result, an incomplete file, or no file at all — dispatch stays blocked while a driver’s file is incomplete. The refusal gives the plain reason, and the hold waits in the exception queue until the file is fixed.

Audit packet, as of any date

One tap builds the complete file as it stood on any chosen date — ready for roadside or audit, without rebuilding it by hand.

Medical status, labelled honestly. A medical certificate on file reads “on file — electronic verification not connected” until a real verification source is wired. The Desk records the Clearinghouse queries the fleet itself ran — it does not look a driver up itself.
Fleet calendar · Live

Every driver’s week on one grid

The fleet calendar puts every driver’s week on one grid for dispatch and the owner — the same loads, home time and resets the driver sees on their own calendar, laid out across the whole fleet so the desk plans the week, not one phone call at a time.

One grid for dispatch and the owner

Every driver’s week, on one grid. Dispatch works the grid day to day — who is committed to what, who is home, who is on a reset — and the owner sees the same grid as dispatch, plus the owner-only levers below. A company driver sees only their own calendar — never the fleet grid, never anyone else’s.

Assigned — the load lands as committed

One of two dispatch modes the fleet owner picks once. In an Assigned fleet, a posted load lands on the driver’s calendar as committed — the desk has spoken, and the load is the driver’s to run.

Offered — the load waits for the driver’s yes

In an Offered fleet, the load waits as an offer until the driver accepts. A decline sends it straight back to the board it came from and is recorded as a fact, never scored against the driver — a no is information for the desk, not a mark on the driver.

Locked inside the safety window

Inside a fleet-set safety window before pickup, a load locks. The driver asks for a release and dispatch decides — close to pickup, a committed load does not quietly fall off a calendar; it moves only when the desk says so.

Reassignment runs on consent

Dispatch can propose moving a load, with its reason shown — and the move fires only when the current driver agrees. A refusal stands, unless the fleet owner overrides it with a stated reason the driver sees. Dispatch cannot override — that lever belongs to the owner alone.

Time off in an Assigned fleet

Drivers request time off by type — home time, medical or doctor visit (including a DOT physical), family, personal, or a 34-hour reset. In an Assigned fleet, a driver’s time-off request becomes a commitment only when dispatch or the owner approves it — until then it sits on the grid as a request, plainly labelled, so nobody plans around days that were never agreed.

The owner owns the exceptions. Setting the fleet’s dispatch mode — Assigned or Offered — and overriding a driver’s refusal with a stated reason are owner-only levers. Dispatch works the grid; the owner holds the calls dispatch cannot make.
Home time & driver pulse · Live

Home time is a commitment, not a hope

The Desk doesn’t just plan the load — it protects the plan to get home, counts whether it held, and checks in before a driver quietly burns out.

Home-time commitments, enforced in planning

A driver — or their fleet, for them — sets the commitment: home by a date, home every N days, or home on weekends. Before any load binds, claimed or assigned, the app checks the delivery time plus a drive-home allowance against it. A load that would break it stops with the plain math shown. It binds only on an explicit override with a reason, and that override is sealed in the record. A commitment a driver set for themselves can only be overridden by that driver — dispatch cannot override it for them.

Hit rate, counted from sealed records only

Kept, missed and overridden are counted from sealed records only. When the app can’t prove a driver got home, the outcome reads “no home record” — it never guesses. Counts print with their sample sizes. There are no scores.

Pulse check-ins

Every couple of weeks the driver gets three short questions — home time, workload, staying — dismissible, never blocking. The fleet sees averages only when at least 3 drivers answered; an individual driver’s answers are never shown to the fleet, and a driver’s written notes are never shared at all.

“Worth a check-in” signals. Fleets also see plain signals figured from sealed facts — missed home time, long detentions, miles falling off. Facts to check on, not verdicts on a person.
Safety & equipment · Live

Coaching, not punishment — and proof that holds

Camera events, fault codes and the trailer itself now feed the same Desk — handled as coaching and plain facts, with the proof sealed while it is fresh.

Dashcam coaching, on the Desk

A camera partner sends driving events — harsh braking, speeding, following distance, collisions. Each event keeps the partner’s clip reference — the app never hosts the video — the driver notes what happened, and dispatch marks it reviewed / coached. Repeats show as plain pattern facts — no scores.

The exoneration vault

Pin any event and the proof around it — clip reference, duty timeline, GPS summary and inspection records — seals into one evidence packet that stays exactly as pinned, ready if a ticket or a claim ever comes.

Fault codes draft their own work orders

Fault codes are translated into plain language with an urgency — stop now / service soon / watch — and the serious ones automatically draft a work order in the maintenance log. An unknown code is recorded exactly as reported, never given an invented meaning, and service-due flags are figured from the truck’s own sealed readings and labelled estimates.

Smart trailer & reefer proof

Trailer position is always printed with its freshness — never dressed up as live. Reefer temperature is logged against the load, an out-of-range reading alerts the driver and dispatch in-app, and the temperature log rides with the load’s records as delivery proof.

Security

Built like the records matter.
Because they do.

Everything on this page is verified live in the app today — stated plainly.

Live today

What's protecting you now

App PIN, properly hashed

Your app PIN is stored as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash — never in plain text — with lockout after repeated wrong tries, and changing it requires the current PIN.

EIN encrypted at rest

A fleet's EIN is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, shown masked, and revealable only by the owner — every reveal is audited.

Hash-chained records

Trip and load records are hash-chained and pass an integrity check. Alter one record and the chain proves it.

No card numbers, ever

STONEMILES never stores card numbers. Payments run only through licensed processors.

No seed phrases. No private keys.

The app never asks for a seed phrase or a private key — not in a form, not in a chat, not anywhere. Anyone asking on our behalf is running a scam. That includes giveaways: we will never ask for your seed phrase, private key, or password to enter or claim a prize. If you need help, contact the Stonervision team at stonervisionteam@gmail.com.

Official giveaways — verify the CA

The Stonervision team runs giveaways from time to time. Every official giveaway token uses a verified contract address (CA) — always check it against the announcements board on this site or in the app before you take part. If a giveaway is not listed on the announcements board, treat it as unofficial.

$STONER carries risk

$STONER is a digital token. Its price can rise or fall without warning, and it can lose all of its value. Nothing Stonervision says — on this site, in our apps, or anywhere else — is financial advice, and nothing is a promise of profit. Taking part is your own decision and your own risk. HTTPS only, no trackers

Traffic is encrypted end to end, and the app ships with no advertising trackers. Company members can never read a driver's private messages.

Security Pack 2

Live in the app

Security Pack 2 is live and verified in the app (October 23, 2026):

Two-factor authentication

Authenticator-app 2FA, with one-time recovery codes for getting back in if the authenticator is lost.

New-device sign-in alerts

When your account signs in on a new device, you're alerted — so a sign-in you don't recognize gets caught fast.

Active Sessions

The Active Sessions screen shows every device signed in to your account, with Sign Out Everywhere to end them all at once.

Sign out — right in the top bar

The app’s top bar carries a Sign out button right beside the menu. One tap — with a quick confirm — signs out this device.

No one-tap way back in

Once you’ve signed out, the signed-out screen asks for a real credential — your app PIN if you’ve set one, Face ID or fingerprint if you’ve enrolled it, or “Sign in with a different account,” which opens the full sign-in (email + password, Google, or passkey). There is no button that lets you straight back in.

Sign-out sticks

Signing out lasts. It survives closing and reopening the app, and the signed-out screen never shows your account email.

Lost-phone remote lock

Lose the phone and the account can be locked remotely, killing its sessions. The app auto-locks, and wallet, settlements, and exports each require a fresh PIN before they open.

Sealed access audit

Access to records is sealed into an audit trail. Drivers can see a “Who accessed my records” list, and an owner can cut off a departed driver's access with Cut Off Access.

Location-privacy rules

A company sees a driver's location only while that driver is on duty or on a trip. Raw GPS breadcrumbs carry a retention limit and are purged automatically — sealed trip records remain.

Money-movement step-ups. When points conversion and cash-out open at the $STONER launch on November 20, 2026, large conversions and cash-outs will require PIN + 2FA and will show a review hold plainly before anything moves. Conversion and cash-out themselves open only at that launch.

Calendar

Score

Conversion

Every 1,000 points carries $0.25 of value

The rate

Every 1,000 SM Points carries $0.25 of value. When conversion pays, you receive that value in $STONER at the market price at that moment — so the token amount moves with the price, and the dollar value of your points never does. Converted in 1,000-point blocks, minimum 10,000 points — so the 10,000-point minimum pays $2.50 of value in $STONER.

The cap

Conversions are capped at 100,000 points per driver per month — $25.00 of value at the anchor, paid in $STONER at the market price when conversion pays.

The pool

Conversions are paid from the Earning Pool — real balances only. If the pool can't cover a conversion, it queues honestly. Conversions are never minted and never promised unfunded.

Conversion opens at the $STONER launch. Points accumulate from day one; conversion activates when $STONER goes live.
Active account required. Converting points and cashing out require an active paying account in good standing. Your points stay yours if you lapse — non-renewal puts your balance on a 2-week retainer: renew in that window and nothing is lost — vesting resumes, and converting and cash-out unlock after a short 2-week hold from reactivation, as long as the account stays active through the hold. Reactivating starts that 2-week hold, and cancelling during the hold starts a fresh 2-week retainer. After the retainer expires, unvested welcome credits return to the pool and do not come back, but your earned points remain, locked until you reactivate.

House Rules

The rules, posted before the game

Plain language, no fine print hiding underneath:

  1. Refunds claw back rewards. A refund or chargeback takes back the points, the $1.00 yearly credit, and any unvested credits it paid for.
  2. Renewal points land on settled payments only — when the money has actually cleared, not when it was attempted.

  6. Reward pools queue publicly when short — never borrowed, never minted, never quietly skipped.
  7. Annual-first pricing. Every price leads with the yearly price; monthly is the fallback.
  8. Team no-sell window. For the first 30 days after $STONER genesis, the team wallet makes no market sells. Giveaway payouts, pool funding, and spending on upgrades and projects still move — paying to build is spending, not market-selling.
  9. Active account to convert or cash out. Converting points and cashing out require an active paying account in good standing. If a paying account doesn't renew, its balance goes on a 2-week retainer — conversion and cash-out are locked and vesting pauses, but the earned points balance is fully retained. Renew within the 2 weeks and nothing is lost — vesting resumes, and converting and cash-out unlock after a short 2-week hold from reactivation. Reactivating after a non-renewal starts a 2-week hold before conversion and cash-out unlock; the account must stay active through the hold, and cancelling during the hold starts a fresh 2-week retainer. If the retainer expires un-renewed, unvested welcome credits return to the Earning Pool and do not come back — only the earned points balance returns on reactivation, staying retained and locked through the hold, with no further decay.
  10. Yearly price lock. A yearly subscriber's rate is frozen for their full year, even if prices rise.

White paper

STONEMILES by Stonervision

Version 1.3 — November 10, 2026 · STONEMILES — “Every mile, sealed.” Built by a Trucker for Truckers. Updated for the fleet dispatch & Library build — broker doors, desk accept & assign-to-driver, receive-link / on-phone / paper-BOL signing, the receiver’s own copy, and the User Library — and the Nov 6 build set: Atlas, satellite + tilt, trailer package, money tools, 5 languages, extras and grouped dashboard — plus the Nov 6 evening GPS verdict repair (de-crowded map, loading fuel pins, in-bar search typing, green night route line) — and the Nov 7 Android Auto & Cab Mode build: glanceable in-app cab display and Android Auto template screens (Guidance / Stops ahead / Road alerts) previewed in-app. Head-unit Android Auto projection is not live yet and ships only through the Play Store listing. The fleet dispatch chain and the User Library described in §3 are live in the current build.

Download the white paper (.md)

1. Overview

STONEMILES is a GPS trucking platform — Built by a Trucker for Truckers — for owner-operators, company drivers, hotshots, fleets and blockchain users. It combines the tools a driver actually needs on the road — truck-legal routing, hazard alerts, fuel intelligence, load records, trip sheets — with a tamper-evident record layer that seals every trip and load, and a rewards economy (SM Points and $STONER) that pays drivers for verified work.

One line: STONEMILES turns the miles a driver already drives into sealed records, real savings, and rewards that are earned, never printed.

2. The problem

  • Trucking runs on paper-thin margins. Fuel is the industry's biggest cost factor (~$0.48 of the ~$2.34 it costs to run a mile), and most drivers buy it blind — the pump price is not the real price.
  • Records are fragmented: paper trip sheets, photos of BOLs, settlement statements drivers can't verify, IFTA math done by hand at quarter-end.
  • Driver loyalty programs elsewhere pay in points that buy nothing, expire silently, or convert at rates nobody can reach.

3. The product

  • Live GPS + truck routing — live map and speed, truck-legal routing on an editable truck profile (height, weight, length), 3 compared routes scored on miles, fuel, tolls, weather safety, and net pay at the driver's rate ($0.55/mi benchmark). Drive / Explore layout: Map, Satellite and Tilt sit in one slim row above the MPH speed bubble with nothing overlapping the speed readout; search typing stays inside the search bar (no iOS auto-zoom displacement); the route line is blue by day and turns green in the map's night look, with the traffic legend matching.
  • Road alerts — speed limits with overspeed alerts, low bridges, weight limits, truck bans, weigh stations (open/closed only from timestamped driver intel — never invented).
  • Fuel intelligence — Fuel Coach (speed/idle coaching costed in dollars from the driver's own data) and the Net-Price Fuel Planner, which ranks stops by net price (pump price minus the IFTA tax of the state where the fuel will be burned — tax runs ~$0.18/gal in Mississippi to ~$0.97 in California, so pump-price rankings flip across state lines). Per-load fuel plans are generated from the pickup and drop addresses before, during, and after each load. Explore Fuel pins load reliably, including stations the map data records as buildings or areas as well as points — the map-data host gap is worked around in the app.
  • Loads & records — loads added by photo/file with extraction and driver confirmation; Load Tracker (Booked → Pickup sealed → Delivered sealed) with geofence proof-of-delivery seals; document vault; signed DVIR; CAT scale tickets sealed.
  • Fleet dispatch chain & the User Library (live) — the flow runs broker sends → desk accepts → driver assigned → driver runs it → receiver confirms on the link → the delivery seals itself → everything lands in the Library, printable, emailable and downloadable. Brokers reach a fleet two ways: a no-account send door (fleet code or link) that drops a load straight into that one fleet’s desk inbox as an offered load, and broker accounts that post to the public loadboard for owner-operators to grab. The desk accepts and assigns a driver from the fleet desk. At the dock the receiver confirms three ways — the receive link (QR printed on the BOL) on their own phone, signing on the driver’s phone, or signing a printed paper BOL the driver photographs and uploads as the signed POD; the first confirmation closes the delivery, the others show “already confirmed,” and dispatch and the fleet owner see it flip to delivered with the signed proof attached and an exception flag if damage or shortage was noted. After a digital signature, the receiver picks how to keep their own copy — by email, by phone number (they type the number as their opt-in; the app hands the driver’s own phone a ready text carrying a view-only link and the driver sends it from their own number), or as a document to download or print on the spot. The User Library holds loads delivered, statements, fuel tax state by state, filings, uploads and sealed files — every item printable, emailable and downloadable.
  • OS/OW permits — permits scanned through the same confirm-before-save pipeline (approved route, dimensions, valid dates, escorts, curfews, bridge bypasses); Approved-Route Mode locks turn-by-turn to the permit's route with a hard alert on leaving the corridor — and states plainly when a permit route can't be matched to the roads; restriction placards ride on the Drive screen as small chips while a permit load is active; permits are filed as active, completed, and expired next to their loads. Bridge-height alerts show the posted clearance on standard routes and yield to the permit's own bypasses on permitted loads.
  • Atlas & map — Atlas is a 50-state reference (weight limits, rules, DOT contacts), offline and reference-only. The map offers satellite view with tilt in one slim Map · Satellite · Tilt row above the MPH bubble, removable anytime via the “Enhanced map view” switch in Settings; the truck-legal route overlays either view — blue by day, green in the night look.
  • Trailer package — trailer types Dry Van / Reefer / Flatbed / Step Deck / RGN, each with its own pre-trip checklist; reefer cold-chain log; securement calculator; loaded height; axle calculator; dock helper; high-wind advisory.
  • Money tools — IFTA Complete (quarterly miles/fuel by state) and IFTA estimator, Settlement Checker, detention tracking, parking planner, HOS planning clocks, plus the latest batch: document expiry wallet, who-owes-me board, true rate, TONU/layover logger, maintenance countdown and breakdown mode.
  • Extras — route-ahead severe weather with coverage labelled exactly on screen; receiver memory (“What to expect here”); scale tickets sealed to the load plus a Scales finder; tax categories and a per-diem day counter; a night parking layer that shows parking places and never claims live availability.
  • Cab Mode & Android Auto (Nov 7 build) — included in every plan, not a separate add-on and with no separate price. Basic includes the basic version: a glanceable cab display (next turn, speed vs posted limit, ETA, drive clock basics). Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner include the full version: voice directions on the cab display, HOS tile, Stops ahead + Road alerts screens, and auto-open with guidance. The Android Auto template screens — Guidance, Stops ahead, Road alerts — are built and previewed in-app. Head-unit projection is not live yet — it ships through the Play Store listing.
  • Dashboard & languages — 52 tools grouped as Drive / Loads & Money / Truck & Trailer / Records & Taxes / More & Settings, every tool within 2 taps, one name per tool across dashboard, menus and Ask Meca. The full app runs in 5 languages: English, Español, Português, Русский, Українська (Settings → Appearance → App language).
  • Company layer — Owner Portal for fleets: drivers join only with an owner-issued code; the fleet dispatch desk (inbox, accept, assign-to-driver, delivered seals with proof attached); company chat, driver groups and DMs (DMs are private — nobody, including owners, can read another driver's DMs).
  • Connections — ELD connections (Samsara, Motive; read-only sync, ELD odometer as miles of record; premium tiers), Safety Academy courses with sealed completions.

4. The trust layer — sealed records

Every trip and load record is hash-chained: change one byte and the chain breaks. Records can be verified by anyone with the short verification code (Verify-Anywhere — state-level detail only, never a driver's private data). Delivery seals are geofenced; load documents are fingerprinted; each driver holds a portable Reputation Passport (off by default, driver-controlled).

On-chain anchoring and escrow are designed, not live: no record goes on-chain and no funds move on-chain without a separate, explicit go-live decision.

5. SM Points — the rewards system (locked October 23, 2026; updated October 25, 2026)

SM Points are earned for GPS-verified work in the app — and for joining and staying subscribed. A free signup earns 100 SM Points; a new paid subscription earns 1,000 SM Points, and every renewal earns another 1,000 SM Points, landing when payments settle. Those are additional to the driving table below. Points are a score and a currency-in-waiting: they are never sendable or swappable between users — the driver who earns them is the only one who can convert them.

Earning — the perfect day pays 500

Daily taskPoints
Morning Briefing check-in25
Pre-trip DVIR signed50
Trip driven and sealed120
On-time delivery, POD sealed165
Clean driving day (no overspeed)75
Road intel confirmed (first of the day)35
Fuel stop logged10
Post-Trip Debrief reviewed20
Perfect day total500

Plus a clean-week streak bonus of +200. A perfect month is worth ~15,000–15,800 points; a strong real month lands 10,000–12,000.

Plus sealed miles: 1 point per 2.5 sealed miles — about $1.00 of value per 10,000 sealed miles. Free tier earns half. Miles points land outside the daily cap.

On the free Basic plan, sealed work pays half: a sealed trip earns 60 points and an on-time delivery with a sealed POD earns 82 points, instead of 120 and 165. Fuel route and fuel-planner features are paid-tier features. Your points are yours — they never expire, and staying on the free tier never costs you your balance: free-tier SM Points are never forfeited for staying free and are never wiped by any season reset, and a free driver keeps his full balance; converting unlocks when you upgrade to a paying tier, and the retained balance then converts under the normal rules (10,000-point minimum).

Conversion — points to $STONER

  • Rate: every 1,000 SM Points carries $0.25 of value, paid in $STONER at the market price when the conversion pays — so the token amount moves with the price, and the dollar value of your points never does
  • Minimum to convert: 10,000 points, converted in 1,000-point blocks ($2.50 of value at the anchor)
  • Monthly conversion cap: 100,000 points per driver ($25.00 of value at the anchor, paid in $STONER at the market price when conversion pays)
  • Conversions are paid from the Earning Pool (see §7). If the pool cannot cover a conversion, it queues honestly — conversions are never minted and never promised unfunded.

Integrity

Point awards are validated server-side (GPS/geofence checks on delivery seals and intel confirmations), capped daily by the table itself, and a voided delivery seal claws back the points it awarded.

Status: earning is built in; conversion activates at the $STONER launch (November 20, 2026) under the go-live gates in §10. Points accumulate from day one.

6. Welcome credits & vesting

Paid from the Earning Pool — real balances only, queued honestly if the pool is dry:

  • Yearly-subscriber credit: a $1.00 credit, paid in $STONER at the market price when it pays out, for yearly (annual) subscribers only — it is not a free-signup credit. Yearly subscribers get both the 1,000 SM Points and the $1.00 credit; monthly subscribers get the points only. The credit is visible at grant and stays locked for send/swap/sell until the account seals its first GPS trip.
  • First-subscription welcome credit (set by the first paid plan ever; upgrades never top it up; once per account; reverses on refund/chargeback; a promo-priced first subscription earns no welcome credit): Gold $1.00 · Diamond $5.00 · Fleet/Owner $25.00 — each paid in $STONER at the market price when it pays out.
  • Vesting: Gold's $1.00 credit lands whole, with no vesting. Diamond: 25% of the $5.00 credit at first subscription, then the rest in 6 equal monthly tranches. Fleet/Owner: 25% of the $25.00 credit at first subscription, then the rest in 12 equal monthly tranches. Vesting continues only while the subscription stays active; a lapsed plan returns the unvested remainder to the Earning Pool, shown plainly. Wallets always show available vs vesting vs total separately.
  • Referrals: the referrer earns 100 $STONER from the Reward Wallet plus SM Points at their referral level when a referred user's first paid subscription settles. Referral rewards are uncapped — every settled referral pays. The points land only on settled payment, and the referral reward reverses — points and $STONER alike — if the referred subscription refunds or charges back. A referred user does not get the $1.00 yearly credit for signing up — they get it only by becoming a yearly subscriber.

Referral levels

The 100 $STONER per settled referral is paid at every level; levels scale the SM Points rate, set by the referrer's level at the moment the recruit's subscription settles.

Level (active referrals)SM Points per referralMilestone & extras
Spotter — 1–4250No badge
Dispatcher — 5+350+1,000 SM Point milestone bonus at 5 (one-time) · Dispatcher badge
Fleet Builder — 15+500+2,500 SM Point milestone bonus at 15 (one-time) · Fleet Builder badge
Road Captain — 40+750+5,000 SM Point milestone bonus at 40 (one-time) · Road Captain badge · featured profile slot on the STONEMILES Board

Levels count active referrals — recruits whose first paid subscription settled and has not refunded. A refund drops the count; a recruit who cancels after real paid months still counts. Milestones pay once per level reached — re-crossing a threshold after a refund drop does not pay twice. A refund claws back that referral's points at the rate actually paid.

Every level above Spotter carries its own distinct badge — the Dispatcher badge, the Fleet Builder badge, and the Road Captain badge — shown on the driver's profile and on the STONEMILES Board. Spotter carries no badge.

7. Where subscription money goes

Subscription revenue funds operations, driver rewards, token burns, and a locked reserve — allocations are set by company policy. Driver rewards are paid from the Earning Pool (welcome credits, points conversion) and the Reward Wallet (referrals, subscriber giveaway, team-run rewards); the two buckets are distinct and never merged. The locked reserve — the Locker — is fed by both payment paths, its balance is publicly visible ("every coin visible, always"), and it unlocks only on Stonervision's go-live decision. Team-wallet transparency: for the first 30 days after $STONER genesis, the team wallet makes no market sells. Giveaway payouts, pool funding, and spending on upgrades and projects still move — paying to build is spending, not market-selling.

9. Pricing

  • Basic — FREE: core GPS, alerts, trip sheet, 1 route, 1 active trip, Cab Mode — basic version (glanceable cab display: next turn, speed vs posted limit, ETA, drive clock basics).
  • Gold Driver — $99/yr or $9.99/mo: 3 routes, fuel stops & parking — basic (fuel stops along route, list + map, with Love's and Pilot/Flying J toggles; Fuel pins load including stations mapped as buildings/areas; prices from your own fuel log and labelled reported prices with age and source, never presented as live; basic parking pins/list), basic weekly fuel summary, basic per-load pre-trip tips, weather, offline maps, satellite view + tilt in a slim row above the MPH bubble (Enhanced map view switch; route line blue by day, green at night), Atlas 50-state offline reference, trailer profiles with per-trailer checklists, 5 app languages, grouped dashboard, multi-stop, loads by photo, document vault, multiple trips, CHIP market panel, Cab Mode — full version (voice directions on the cab display, HOS tile, Stops ahead + Road alerts screens, auto-open with guidance).
  • Diamond Driver — $199/yr or $19.99/mo: everything in Gold plus parking & fuel assistance — full: full Fuel Coach (live speed/idle coaching + full per-load debriefs), full Net-Price Fuel Planner (net-of-tax ranking, lane fuel plan before/during/after the load, full after-load debrief), full parking assistance (parking along route and end-of-day parking planning tied to the driver's HOS clocks, surfacing options before drive time runs out; parking intel/reports; saved spots; night parking layer — places, not live availability), full trailer package (reefer cold-chain log, securement calculator, loaded height, axle calculator, dock helper, high-wind advisory), full money tools (document expiry wallet, who-owes-me board, true rate, TONU/layover logger, IFTA estimator, maintenance countdown, breakdown mode), extras (route-ahead severe weather with labelled coverage, receiver memory, scale tickets + Scales finder, tax categories + per-diem counter), OS/OW Permit Mode (permit scan, approved-route driving, restriction placards, permit file), ELD connections, Safety Academy + owner videos, Settlement Checker, white-glove import, priority help, Cab Mode — full version.
  • Fleet/Owner — $499/yr annual ($49.99/mo flat up to 3 trucks; $599.88/yr billed monthly), first dispatch seat included, the owner pays $99/yr per extra driver or dispatch seat on annual ($9.99/mo billed monthly) — that covers the seat's subscription, so drivers and dispatchers on the plan pay nothing themselves. Owner-plan drivers get Diamond included, Cab Mode — full version for every driver on the plan, the fleet dispatch desk, and the fleet's User Library.
  • Cab Mode / Android Auto — no separate price: Cab Mode is tiered inclusion, not an add-on. Basic includes the basic version; Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner include the full version. Head-unit projection is not live yet — it ships through the Play Store listing.

Pricing is annual-first everywhere: the yearly price leads, monthly is the fallback. Yearly price lock: a yearly subscriber's rate is frozen for their full year, even if prices rise. Billing activates at app-store release; there is no fake checkout.

10. $STONER, the wallet, and CHIP

  • $STONER (name "stonervision", ticker "stoner", supply 1,000,000,000) launches November 20, 2026 as the genesis launch on CHIP, the launchpad operated by Chief's Investing Plaza on Robinhood Chain (4663). The CHIP partnership agreement was fully executed October 23, 2026 (2% launchpad fee; independent audit draft due November 10; no genesis with open critical or high findings).
  • In-app wallet: custodial wallet created at signup (labelled honestly as custodial; an own-wallet connect option is offered; seed phrases and private keys are never requested). Chains: Robinhood Chain (home of $STONER), Solana, Bitcoin, Polygon, Sui. Outside-chain assets swap into $STONER only, with bridge/swap fees itemized before confirming.
  • On/off ramps: fiat purchases front-load identity verification (KYC at buy, so cash-out is fast later): instant cash-out to debit card / Cash App for paid subscribers (provider fee itemized; provider fraud holds shown plainly), standard ACH (1–3 business days) for everyone — all through licensed providers, staged off until provider agreements and the go-live decision land.
  • In-app swap (STONERxSWAP design, Uniswap v4, 1% fee, shown before you sign, never holds keys) is built and staged off until the separate on-chain go-live approval.

11. Roadmap

  • Nov 9–11, 2026: first live road test in the cab (mileage tracker + STONEMILES).
  • Nov 10, 2026: independent CHIP audit draft due.
  • Nov 20, 2026: $STONER genesis on CHIP; launch giveaway drawn; subscriber giveaway and points conversion activate under go-live gates.
  • Fleet dispatch & the Library (live in the current build): broker send door + broker loadboard accounts, desk accept and assign-to-driver, receive-link / on-phone / paper-BOL signing with the receiver’s own copy, self-sealing deliveries, and the User Library (loads delivered, statements, fuel tax state by state, filings, uploads, sealed files — print, email, download).
  • Cab Mode (build landed Nov 7, 2026): Cab Mode is included by tier — basic version in Basic, full version in Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner — with no separate Cab Mode price. The glanceable in-app cab display and the Android Auto template screens (Guidance / Stops ahead / Road alerts) are built and previewed in-app.
  • Android Auto: Head-unit projection is not live yet — it ships through the Play Store listing.
  • CarPlay — later, on Apple’s road: Apple Developer membership Dec 4, 2026, then an iOS build of STONEMILES, then Apple’s separate CarPlay navigation entitlement approval.
  • Then: native app wrap (Capacitor) with true background GPS on iOS/Android; app-store submission as an organization; commercial routing provider; lock-for-perks (voluntary $STONER locking for perks — design approved as a direction, mechanics set later).

12. Honest limits

Staged and labelled as such in the app, never presented as live: on-chain anchoring and escrow (design only), in-app swap, cash-out lanes, subscription billing (starts at app-store release), points conversion (activates at launch), and head-unit Android Auto projection — the template screens are built and previewed in-app, but projection itself ships only through the Play Store listing after Google’s identity review, the native build and Google’s Android Auto review; CarPlay likewise awaits the Dec 4 Apple membership, an iOS build and Apple’s entitlement approval. Fuel prices in the planner come from the driver's own fuel log, driver-reported prices (age- and source-labelled), and weekly EIA regional averages — never presented as live station prices. The night parking layer shows parking places only and never claims live availability. Route-ahead weather coverage is labelled on screen for what is and is not covered. Atlas is reference-only and does not replace permits, signage or state law. Traffic is shown as unavailable where no real feed exists. Privacy Policy

STONEMILES by Stonervision · Effective October 23, 2026

What we collect

  • Account details — your name, email address, company details, and role (owner, dispatch, or driver).
  • GPS location while on duty / on a trip — location is collected while you are on duty or running a trip in the app, to provide routing, trip records, IFTA state-line logging, and delivery geofence seals.
  • Trip and document records — the trips, loads, documents, and records you create or upload in the app, including the sealed records generated from them.

How we use it

Your information is used to operate STONEMILES: routing and guidance, trip sheets and IFTA reporting, load and delivery records, fleet coordination for companies you belong to, rewards for GPS-verified work, and support.

What we never do

  • Your location is never sold.
  • Wallet data is never included in exports. Trip, fleet, and IFTA exports never contain wallet data.
  • STONEMILES carries no advertising trackers, and the app never asks for a seed phrase or private key.

Companies and your data

If you drive for a company on STONEMILES, the company can see the fleet records for its own operation. Company members can never read a driver's private messages.

Your control

  • Drivers control their data and can wipe it in-app.
  • Account deletion is available on request by email — write to the Stonervision team email, stonervisionteam@gmail.com, and we will delete your account and its data.

Terms of Use

STONEMILES by Stonervision · Effective October 23, 2026

What STONEMILES is

STONEMILES is a planning and record-keeping aid for trucking businesses and drivers — routing, trip records, fuel planning, and related tools.

Not a certified ELD

STONEMILES is not a certified ELD unless connected to a certified provider (such as a connected Samsara or Motive ELD). Where an ELD connection is active, the certified provider's system remains the ELD of record.

Your responsibilities

  • The driver remains responsible for hours-of-service compliance at all times, regardless of any planning clocks, summaries, or estimates shown in the app.
  • Routing is guidance. Road conditions, signage, and posted restrictions on the ground govern — if the road disagrees with the route, the road wins.
  • On a permitted load, the permit itself governs: Approved-Route Mode follows the route on your OS/OW permit, and you remain responsible for travelling only within the permit's dates, dimensions, escort, and curfew terms.
  • You are responsible for the accuracy of documents and information you add to your records.

Accounts and companies

Drivers join a company only with an owner-issued code. Owners are responsible for the seats and access they issue under their company account.

Subscriptions

Pricing is as published on the Pricing page and is locked, shown annual-first with monthly as the fallback. A yearly subscriber's rate is frozen for their full year, even if prices rise. Billing begins at app-store release; no charges are made before then. Payments are processed only through licensed processors — STONEMILES never stores card numbers.

Rewards

SM Points are earned for GPS-verified activity — plus 100 SM Points at free signup, 1,000 when a paid subscription starts, and 1,000 at every renewal (landing when payments settle). Points are never sendable or swappable between users, and every 1,000 points carries $0.25 of value, paid in $STONER at the market price when the conversion pays. Free-tier SM Points never expire, are never forfeited for staying free, and are never wiped by any season reset — a free driver keeps his full balance; converting unlocks when you upgrade to a paying tier, and the retained balance then converts under the normal rules (10,000-point minimum). The $1.00 credit, paid in $STONER at the market price when it pays out, is for yearly subscribers only. Referrals: when a referred user's first paid subscription settles, the referrer earns 100 $STONER from the Reward Wallet plus SM Points at their referral level; referral points rates and milestones are set by the referrer's level under the posted levels table. Referral rewards are uncapped, the points land only on settled payment, and the referral reward reverses if the referred subscription refunds or charges back. Converting points and cashing out require an active paying account in good standing. Your points stay yours if you lapse: when a paying account doesn't renew, its balance goes on a 2-week retainer — conversion and cash-out are locked and vesting pauses, but the earned points balance is fully retained. Renew within the 2 weeks and nothing is lost — vesting resumes, and converting and cash-out unlock after a short 2-week hold from reactivation. Reactivating after a non-renewal starts a 2-week hold before conversion and cash-out unlock; the account must stay active through the hold, and cancelling during the hold starts a fresh 2-week retainer. If the retainer expires un-renewed, unvested welcome credits return to the Earning Pool and do not come back — only the earned points balance returns on reactivation, staying retained and locked through the hold, with no further decay. Welcome credits and the House Rules are governed by the terms published on the $STONER & Rewards page and in the white paper. Points and $STONER are rewards mechanics, not financial products, and nothing in STONEMILES is financial advice.
